overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the April 10 notice was specific enough, the breakfasts and March dinner showed no deliberation by a quorum, and the Town Meeting jurisdiction claim was declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 10 notice was too vague because it did not say the Board would vote to join a regional emergency communications district.
allegations.key_passage: We have found in prior determinations that, even where the topic notice does not indicate that a vote will take place, the possibility of a vote is reasonably foreseeable.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Board members deliberated outside a noticed meeting through breakfast events and a March dinner attended by all members with the town administrator.
allegations.key_passage: While the town administrator, who is not a Board member, met with individual Board members on two occasions at breakfast events, this did not constitute deliberation between or among a quorum.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the regional communications center decision should have gone to Town Meeting because it affects town finances, not the Board.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation because, even if true, this claim would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law
